read_evidence.behavior_explained: The four sites have two different legacy formulas. Hunks 1 and 4 store the quotient in float loc_xyz, decrement negative values, then convert to int64_t (truncation toward zero). For exactly representable examples, x=-1.5 gives int(-2.5)=-2, equal to floor(-1.5), but x=-2 gives -3 instead of floor(-2)=-2. Thus this formula is not floor(x)-1 for every negative quotient; floating-point rounding near boundaries also needs care. Hunks 2 and 3 instead use int loc_xyz already assigned floor(x), then subtract one extra unit for negative x, yielding floor(x)-1. The patch makes the former sites use floor and removes the latter extra decrements, unifying insertion/retrieval keys. Potential key mismatches follow from the differing formulas; no runtime missed/duplicated-update rate was measured.

read_evidence.behavior_explained: Two hunks in Fast DDS 2.14.6 src/cpp/rtps/transport/shared_mem/SharedMemGlobal.hpp implement the two-sided SHM health handshake. Listener side: keep the closed/data fast paths, then call empty_cv.timed_wait(lock, timeout) without a predicate so a health-check notify that carries no data still refreshes the listener heartbeat, and re-check closed/head afterwards. Checker side (healthy_check failure path): empty_cv.notify_all() to ask idle listeners for fresh liveness evidence, then sleep 1 ms instead of the full port_wait_timeout_ms. Data/close fast paths, the total health timeout (healthy_check_timeout_ms = 1000), reliable QoS and the SHM+UDP topology are unchanged.
read_evidence.hunk_locations: 2 hunks: listener wait loop (~line 593) and checker retry sleep (~line 891)
